what: Tracker Cleaner against the tracking lab: measured, nothing demanded. status: tracked = arrived and tied to the person; unlinked = arrived, not tied to her; stopped = nothing arrived (C: after the manual cleaning). Three counts, of the 35 kinds built (one of 36, T34, is not built in the lab): arrived = it arrived at all, also tied to nobody. ever = it arrived, tied to her (in Q and C: after the answers or the cleaning, on the second look). atEnd = it still arrived, tied to her, after Chrome was started again; or, for a kind the trip only makes before that, the last time the trip made it (reference.lastChance); or, for a kind kept in Chrome's own files, it is still in the files when the trip is over; in C, a kind the second look makes again counts when it arrived then. The headline is A (the fresh install, no press) and Q (the same with every question answered yes).
headline: A (fresh install, nothing changed), of the 35 kinds built: 22 at the end; 24 arrived and tied to her; 27 arrived at all; T18, T19 kept on purpose: your own history, readable by no website. Q (fresh install, every question answered yes: Remove, Skip it, cut it off; nothing else by hand): 6 at the end; 8 tied to her after the answers; 24 arrived at all; T18, T19 kept on purpose: your own history, readable by no website. B0 (every group forced to Automatic): 22 at the end; 24 arrived and tied to her; 27 arrived at all; T18, T19 kept on purpose: your own history, readable by no website. B: 6 at the end; 9 arrived and tied to her; 9 arrived at all; T18, T19 kept on purpose: your own history, readable by no website. C (lab names entered, every question answered yes and every manual cleaning done): 5 at the end; 7 tied to her after the cleaning; 9 arrived at all; T18, T19 kept on purpose: your own history, readable by no website.
caveats: Nothing is cut short in the measurement any more: there is no hold on everything (L4). The lab's own "Sign in with" page holds deleting for the network's own site for five minutes, as it would for a user.
A is the fresh install with no press; Q is the same with every question the extension asks answered yes; since L1 a company on no list is not even blocked without such a press.
In Q each press is a message sent to the extension from its own popup page, the message the button sends; it is not a click on the button in the report.
The numbers differ from run to run by a few kinds (seen: "arrived at all" 15 to 28 for the same setting): how many requests get through before a block depends on timing.
The lab does not use the fingerprint to tie visits together, so the page shield is not measured by these numbers.
T18 and T19 (site icons and history) are counted apart as her own history, readable by no website.
T22 (notification right) is counted apart when it arrives only through the lab's simulated press on Allow.
One kind of 36 (T34) is not built in the lab.

settings.A: fresh install defaults, nothing approved, no lab entries
settings.Q: as A, and every question the extension asks is answered with its yes (Remove, Skip it, cut it off), each by its own press, when a user would see it: at the start of the step after the one in which it appeared (the badge is up by then), and once more after the last step; nothing else by hand; then the sites again
settings.B0: main switch on, every group that can run here forced to Automatic, also those that ask on a fresh install (Google's identity cookies, storage and permissions of the user's own lists); no lab entries (the lab is on no list)
settings.B: as B0, with the lab's test-only entries
settings.C: as B, then every manual action at the end (approve all, drop each lab site's cookies and storage, block the permission, clear the cache), then the sites again

recognised: Not recognised as shipped: none of the lab's site names is in DOMAINS or rules.json, none of its cookie names matches COOKIE_RE, and ffclid is not in URL_PARAMS (only the canary's utm_source is).

testOnlyEntries.how: B and C only, alive only while the script runs; no shipped file is edited
testOnlyEntries.notAdded: DOMAINS (cookies judged by tracker host) is a constant inside lists.js, so the always-delete list by cookie name stands in for it. Permanent storage and permission drops come only from the settings program on port 8088, which is not running and is not imitated: in C they are done by hand instead.

simulated: nothing is cut short: there is no hold on everything any more; the lab's own sign-in page holds deleting for the network's own site for five minutes

simulatedRows.T22: the lab's Allow is a grant over the control channel and overrides every setting, so the lab reads "granted" whatever the cleaner does. When Chrome's real setting for that site (contentSettings, read from the extension at the end) is "block", T22 is not counted at the end and is listed in counts.simulated

ownRecord: T18 and T19 are the user's own history and site icons in Chrome's files, readable by no website; the trip hands them to the lab from outside. Still in the files at the end, they are not counted at the end and are listed in counts.own. C presses "Clear my browsing history" with its other manual actions, before the second look

groupsLeftAlone.tor: would send requests off this computer
groupsLeftAlone.tabs: would close the trip's own tabs
groupsLeftAlone.allowlist: needs a list from the settings program; would delete every cookie
groupsLeftAlone.wifi: never automatic; touches this computer's saved networks, so it is not approved either
